descriptor: Rajkot forging and machining SME, listed Jul 2026
lede: A Rajkot maker of closed-die forged and machined parts (rings, ball studs, gear blanks, gears) for tractor, auto and industrial OEMs in India and Europe. It listed on NSE Emerge on 28 Jul 2026 after a ₹50 Cr fresh issue at ₹77 and now trades at about twice that. Revenue has grown ~27% a year with margins above 20%, but working capital is heavy, cash flow is weak and there is no track record as a listed company yet.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹95.5 Cr (+28%), EBITDA margin 23% (14% in FY24), PAT ₹12.4 Cr. Plants run at 90% and IPO money funds a 29% forging-capacity increase by Mar 2028; exports are 35% of revenue.

₹26 Cr of profit over FY23-26 against ₹4 Cr of operating cash flow; inventory days rose to 257. Top customer 23% and top ten 65% of revenue. Order book only ₹27.6 Cr. No call or presentation yet; a Pune plant was approved two months after listing without details.
~32x FY26 earnings, above Rolex Rings (24x) and M M Forgings (23x), below Happy Forgings (54x).

blocks.text: Metalic forges steel billets into near-net shapes on hammers and a 300-ton screw press, heat-treats them, and machines them into finished rings, ball studs, gears and coupling parts in three units at Padavala, Rajkot. It sells to OEMs of tractors, cars, commercial vehicles and farm, hydraulic and construction equipment; Germany alone was 21% of FY26 revenue.

items.text: Gear cutting, grinding and machining in-house let it sell finished parts, not just forgings; EBITDA margin rose from 14% in FY24 to 23% in FY26.
Job work is outsourced at peak load; bringing it in-house is a stated aim of the capex.
Revenue from ₹47 Cr (FY23) to ₹96 Cr (FY26).
16:1 bonus issue in Mar 2026, then a ₹49.96 Cr IPO in Jul 2026 (64.88 lakh shares at ₹77).
Board approved leasing premises in Pune for new manufacturing on 25 Sep 2026; terms not final.

items.text: Seven promoters (Gajipara, Trambadiya, Vadodariya, Kapadiya and Rupapara families) hold 61.0%; domestic institutions 10.1%; 769 shareholders.
No pledge shown.
Siddheshwar Technoforge, a group company, is a supplier and job-worker (₹0.7 Cr in FY26) in the same business, a possible conflict.
₹3.3 Cr of machinery was bought from group firm Motiontech in FY25; advances to group firms (₹1.4 Cr outstanding at Mar 2025) were repaid by Mar 2026.
Directors' pay is modest (₹0.99 Cr in FY26), plus ₹0.78 Cr of salaries to promoters and relatives.
Only one small tax case (₹5.8 lakh) outstanding.

items.label: EV / FY26 EBITDA, before IPO cash

blocks.text: Metalic has grown quickly with good margins for a small forger, and the IPO money funds its next step. At about twice the IPO price and above larger peers' multiples, the stock prices in growth that has not yet shown up in cash. The first listed results, the use of IPO money and the Pune plant details will show whether management does what the prospectus says.
